prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so I give the best recommendations:
- How badly were you injured (minor, moderate, serious)?  
- Was the other driver clearly at fault? Were police/ambulance involved?  
- Do you already have a claim number with an insurer?  
- Do you want a local Pleasanton lawyer specifically, or are you okay with an East Bay/Alameda County firm?  

What I can do right away
- Tell you what to do now (important deadlines and preservation steps).  
- Explain how to choose the right personal-injury lawyer and what to ask at a free consultation.  
- If you want, I can pull together a short list of local Pleasanton / East Bay personal-injury attorneys and resources (I’ll need your zip code or permission to search Pleasanton + nearby cities).

Immediate steps (do these now if you haven’t)
1. Get medical care and follow prescribed treatment. Document everything.  
2. Call the police (if not already done) and get the collision report number.  
3. Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; names/phone numbers of witnesses.  
4. Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer and don’t sign medical release forms or settlement papers without advice.  
5. Report the crash to your own insurer as required by your policy.  
6. Keep a folder of all medical bills, pay stubs (for lost wages), receipts, and correspondence.  
7. Note: California’s general personal-injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the date of injury (Code of Civil Procedure § 335.1). Suits against government entities have much shorter deadlines (often 6 months for a claim) — act faster if a public agency is involved.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for:
- Focus on car accidents / personal injury (not just general practice).  
- Trial and settlement experience — many cases settle, but you want someone who will try the case if needed.  
- Track record of results for injuries similar to yours (fractures, back/neck, TBI, etc.).  
- Works on contingency fee (common) — ask exact percentage and whether costs are advanced.  
- Good communication: who will handle your file day-to-day, how often you’ll get updates.  
- Local knowledge of Alameda County courts and medical providers.  
- Clean disciplinary record (check State Bar).  
- Clear fee agreement and how medical liens/specialists are handled.

Questions to ask at the free consultation
- What percentage of your practice is auto accident/personal injury?  
- How many cases like mine have you handled, and what were the outcomes?  
- Who will handle the case day-to-day? Will it be you or junior staff?  
- What is your fee structure and who pays case costs if we don’t win?  
- Do you handle medical liens and treatment referrals?  
- What’s a realistic timeline and likely value range for my case?  
- Do you take cases to trial? How many jury trials have you tried?  
- Can you provide recent client references or examples (anonymized)?

Where to search and check credentials
- State Bar of California “Attorney Search” (discipline and license status).  
- Review sites: Avvo, Super Lawyers, Google/Yelp (read multiple reviews).  
- Local Alameda County Bar Association referrals.  
- Ask friends/family for personal recommendations.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 4–6 Pleasanton / East Bay personal-injury attorneys/firms that take car-accident cases, with short notes on experience, ratings, and phone numbers. (Tell me your zip code or confirm Pleasanton + nearby cities are OK.)  
- Draft an email or script you can use when calling firms to set up consultations.

Tell me how you want to proceed (I recommend getting 2–3 free consultations and comparing answers).
